question: Which Cluster III names in the DENR-NCR 2025 Pasig River system management list have independent official name/locality support, and which entries remain ambiguous?
method: Compared only the ten Cluster III labels already reviewed in the linked DENR-NCR Annual Report 2025 scope artifact with independent official city and DENR-NCR text. Exact-name support, orthographic difference, and ambiguous administrative/monitoring labels were kept separate. The city sources establish textual name and broad locality context only; no geometry or taxon claims were inferred.

rightsDecision.decision: Keep findings as short attributed internal research notes. Official hosting does not establish a blanket redistribution license; do not publish source maps, tables, or derived geometries from this batch.

limitations: The annual report gives cluster-level administrative context, not an individual locality for every Cluster III entry.
Name-level source support does not establish a unique channel identity, precise route, bank boundary, catchment, habitat condition, fish occurrence, fishing access, legality, or safety.
The source spelling “Ermitanyo” and Mandaluyong’s “Ermitaño” remain an orthographic candidate and were not merged.
Makati’s “Sta. Clara Creek” and DENR-NCR’s “Estero de Sta. Clara” are retained as a possible name relationship, not a confirmed physical-feature identity.
Makati uses “Guadalupe Nuevo” as a barangay and “Guadalupe Nuevo Station” as a monitoring-site label; no separate waterway identity was corroborated in this bounded search.
The cluster is a selected management list, not a complete inventory of NCR waterways or fish habitats.
No water quality, fish, access, legal, hazard, geometry, or public-app claims are admitted.
